question: Who is the Chief Executive Head of the State?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Governor** is the Chief Executive Head of the State.
 
• According to the **Constitution of India**, the Governor is appointed by the **President of India**.
 
• The Governor acts as the representative of the central government in the state.
 
• The **Governor's duties** include overseeing the functioning of the state government, ensuring that the state government acts within the framework of the Constitution, and having the power to summon and dissolve the state legislative assembly.
 
• The Governor also has the authority to appoint the **Chief Minister** and other members of the state council of ministers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Governor** holds office for a term of **five years** but can remain in office until a successor is appointed.
 
• The Governor can be reappointed or transferred to another state by the President.
 
• The powers and functions of the Governor are similar to those of the President of India at the state level.
 
• The Governor plays a crucial role in the administration and governance of the state, including giving assent to bills passed by the state legislature, issuing ordinances when the legislature is not in session, and ensuring that the state government adheres to the provisions of the Constitution.
